newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 23.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Greenbelt in Seoul to be remapped, deregulating some 270,000 square meters and easing construction regulations on 3.23 million square meters.
- Cold spell hits nation: mercury in Seoul plunges to minus five C.

- Extraordinary parliamentary session due today to act on government-initiated intelligence agency law bill. Opposition camp is poised to block the bill's passage, foreshadowing a clash with the ruling New Korea party.

- Korean Ambassador to Peru Lee Won-young, having been conditionally released by Peruvian guerrillas from the Japanese embassy in Lima, will not to return to the hostage site. Most hostages are expected to be freed step by step.

- The Korea Fair Trade Commission will allow department stores to hold discount sales all year round beginning in April next year. Currently, discount sales period are limited to 15 days every two months days for yearly discount sales.
- Fujimori urges rebels to free hostages. Rebels promise more releases after Peruvian government rules out armed rescue.
